column2: Strawberries can cause a rash in some babies; offer a small amount the first time.
Courgette bulgur pilaf (baby)
2 tablespoons fine pilaf bulgur
Grate the courgette; peel and grate the tomato.
Sauté the courgette in olive oil for 2 minutes and add the tomato.
Add the bulgur and hot water and cook over low heat for 12–15 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Leave covered for 10 minutes to steam.
Serve lukewarm; mash a little with a fork if needed.
Bulgur contains iron and fibre.
Chickpea and courgette hummus (baby)
3 tablespoons well-cooked chickpeas
1 teaspoon tahini
Dice the courgette and steam for 8 minutes until soft.
Remove the chickpea skins and put the chickpeas in the blender with the courgette.
Add the tahini, olive oil and lemon juice.
Blend until smooth; add boiled water if needed.
Serve with a spoon or spread on soft steamed vegetable sticks.
Tahini contains sesame; sesame is an allergenic food.
If using tinned chickpeas, rinse off the salt thoroughly.
Homemade wholemeal breadsticks
Mix the flours, yeast, olive oil and lukewarm water and knead into a soft dough.
Cover and leave to rise for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll into pencil-thick sticks.
Place on a tray lined with baking paper and bake for 15–18 minutes until light golden.
Cool completely before serving.
No salt added; suitable for teething children, but stay with them while they eat.
You can add grated carrot or spinach purée to the dough.
Mini turkey and vegetable meatballs
150 g minced turkey
Finely grate the carrot and courgette and squeeze out the liquid.
Knead all the ingredients together for 2–3 minutes.
Shape meatballs slightly bigger than a hazelnut and place on the tray.
Bake for 15–18 minutes until the meatballs are cooked right through.
Once lukewarm, halve to check and serve.
There must be no pink inside the mince.
Don’t add salt; the thyme gives flavour.
Peach yoghurt pudding
Peel and stone the peach and purée it.
Whisk the milk and rice flour together while cold.
Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 6–7 minutes until thickened.
Take off the heat and, once lukewarm, stir in the peach purée.
Divide between bowls and serve topped with yoghurt.
Cow’s milk is not given as a main drink before 12 months; here it is used cooked in a recipe.
Don’t add sugar; the fruit sweetens it.
Baked vegetable pasta (child)
100 g small pasta
3 tablespoons grated unsalted cheese
Boil the pasta in unsalted water for the packet time; add the finely chopped broccoli and carrot for the last 4 minutes and drain.
Melt the butter and cook the flour for 1 minute; add the milk gradually, stirring until thickened.
Mix the sauce with the pasta and vegetables and transfer to a small ovenproof dish.
Sprinkle with the cheese and bake for 15 minutes until golden on top.
Chop the vegetables small so children can’t pick them out.
Don’t add salt; the cheese is salty enough.
Mini apple and carrot muffins
6 tablespoons wholemeal flour
Preheat the oven to 180°C and grease the mini muffin tin.
Finely grate the apple and carrot.
Whisk the egg, yoghurt and olive oil; add the apple and carrot.
Add the flour, baking powder and cinnamon and stir a few times.
Divide between the moulds and bake for 15–18 minutes until a toothpick comes out dry.
No added sugar; the sweetness comes from the fruit.
Handy for travel and the nursery bag.
